title: UAE Logistics Brief
lede: The war has opened a second front on Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast: the Houthis threatened Jeddah and every Saudi Red Sea port, and Jazan and Jeddah were struck on Wednesday night. Inside the Gulf, a projectile exploded near a tanker 50 nautical miles off Dubai and Iran says two more tankers hit mines, while airfreight rates rose for a seventh week.

gauges.label: Global average airfreight rate, 9–15 Nov
gauges.note: Seventh weekly rise; Middle East & South Asia rates up 62% year on year (WorldACD via Air Cargo News)

gauges.label: Hormuz oil flows vs pre-war
gauges.note: Kpler: 8.64m barrels a day in the week to 15 Nov against 17.15m before the war (via Marketcalls)

gauges.label: Gulf war-risk cover, share of hull value per transit
gauges.note: About 0.25% before the war (Lloyd's List and Marsh, via Marketcalls)

gauges.label: Brent crude settle, 24 Nov
gauges.note: Up 2.27% on the day; around $91 late on 25 Nov (Political.org; InvestingLive)

gauges.note: Up 24% year on year; net profit Dh48m, up 817% (Khaleej Times, 10 Nov)

stories.headline: Houthis threaten all Saudi Red Sea ports; Jazan and Jeddah struck
body: On 25 November the Houthis said Jeddah and every other Saudi Red Sea port would be targeted if Saudi Arabia attacks Hodeidah. They told port workers to evacuate and shipping lines to pull their vessels out. The Saudi-led coalition then said it hit targets in Hodeidah, Saada and Amran.

Late on Wednesday the coalition said a projectile hit Jazan port, causing minor damage, and a drone was shot down over Jeddah port. Since Hormuz closed in March, Saudi Arabia has relied on Jeddah and Yanbu for key imports and non-oil exports.
stories.soWhat: New: the Red Sea back door into Saudi is now a target too. UAE-to-Saudi road freight becomes the safest way into the Kingdom; price and sell it that way.

stories.headline: Projectile explodes near tanker 50 miles off Dubai; Iran says two more tankers hit mines
body: UKMTO said a tanker reported an explosion from an unknown projectile close to the ship, about 50 nautical miles west of Dubai, at 21:30 GMT on 25 November. The crew are safe and no damage was reported.

Earlier on Wednesday Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers hit mines and caught fire in the strait while using an unauthorised route. Iran warned ships that do not coordinate with its forces face greater risk. The claims are not independently verified.
stories.soWhat: New: the attacks have moved inside the Gulf, close to Jebel Ali's approaches. Expect insurers and lines to treat Dubai calls as higher risk; keep sea quote validity short.

stories.headline: Hormuz oil flows at half; war-risk cover up to 9% of hull value
body: Kpler data put oil through Hormuz at 8.64 million barrels a day in the week to 15 November, against 17.15 million before the war. AIS-visible traffic was about 9% of the pre-war rate as of 24 November.
Lloyd's List data put Gulf war-risk cover at 7% to 9% of hull value per transit, against about 0.25% before the war.
stories.soWhat: War-risk cost is now a major part of every Gulf sea move. Show it as a separate line in quotes so customers see where the price comes from.

stories.headline: Airfreight rates rise for a seventh week; Middle East up 62% on last year
body: WorldACD's worldwide average rate rose 2% to $3.49 per kg in the week of 9–15 November, up from $3.04 in mid-September. Global rates are 32% above last year, and Middle East & South Asia shows the biggest rise at 62%.
Rates from the region slipped 1% on the week as its capacity fell 1%. WorldACD expects only restrained increases from here.
stories.soWhat: Air remains expensive but is flattening from our region. Hold air express prices; avoid locking long contracts at today's peak.
stories.imageCredit: tratong / Shutterstock via Air Cargo News

stories.headline: noon's Yellow Friday runs to 30 November with 15-minute delivery on Minutes
body: noon's 12-day Yellow Friday sale runs from 19 to 30 November across noon, noon Minutes, noon Food and supermall, with discounts of up to 90%.
noon Minutes offers up to 80% off, and selected orders can arrive in as little as 15 minutes. It overlaps fully with Amazon's White Friday, which also ends on 30 November.
stories.soWhat: Both big marketplaces peak until Sunday. The parcels that do not go through noon's own fleet are open to us: chase sellers now and line up December returns.

competitors.name: Emirates SkyCargo
competitors.headline: MoU with Virgin Atlantic Cargo to widen block space and interline deals
body: Emirates SkyCargo and Virgin Atlantic Cargo signed an MoU to explore wider interline and block space agreements. Emirates gains reach across the Americas, Virgin across the Middle East and Asia.
For the first time it would allow interlining of active pharma shipments such as vaccines and insulin. The two moved a combined 2,000 tonnes in the first half of 2026.
competitors.soWhat: More Dubai–Americas capacity via London could ease our air buying. Ask for a block space offer and look at a healthcare lane to the US.
competitors.imageCredit: Emirates SkyCargo via Air Cargo News

competitors.name: Keeta Drone (Meituan)
competitors.headline: Shows villa drone drops in Dubai, but no start date
body: Keeta Drone flew a package from Sobha Hartland to the Museum of the Future on 18 November, under Dubai Civil Aviation Authority supervision. No launch date has been set.
The drone carries up to 4.5 kg over 20 km one way. Keeta says it has done over 880,000 drone deliveries in China and Dubai.
competitors.soWhat: Drone delivery is not a near-term threat to parcels, but Keeta is building a Dubai last-mile network. Watch it for light, urgent B2C items.

competitors.name: DHL
competitors.headline: Moving closer to Khor Fakkan and Fujairah; Gulf plan stays at €500m
body: DHL Global Forwarding plans to strengthen its position in the east of the UAE, near Khor Fakkan, Dibba and Fujairah. Its €500 million Gulf investment is unchanged, and it has a 20-year joint venture with Etihad Rail for UAE freight.
MEA CEO Tobias Maier expects logistics to take three to six months to normalise after the war ends.
competitors.soWhat: Context for this week's east-coast attacks: DHL is betting on the same gateways we use. Lock in east-coast warehouse and trucking capacity before it is taken. (Story from 8 Nov.)

competitors.name: Aramex (baseline)
competitors.headline: Record Q3: revenue up 24% to Dh1.98bn, profit Dh48m
body: Q3 net profit rose 817% to Dh48 million and revenue rose 24% to a record Dh1.98 billion. Freight forwarding drove the growth.
Gross margin was 21%, down from 23.2% a year earlier.
competitors.soWhat: Volume is strong but margin is thinner. Price the war-risk and surcharge costs through rather than absorbing them.

opportunities.title: UAE–Saudi road as the safe gate
opportunities.text: Saudi Red Sea ports are now threatened and Saudi air cargo is already down. Road freight and road express from the UAE are the steady route into the Kingdom.

opportunities.title: Marketplace peak to Sunday
opportunities.text: noon's Yellow Friday and Amazon's White Friday both run to 30 November. Offer overflow capacity to sellers now and a returns rate for December.

opportunities.title: Healthcare air to the Americas
opportunities.text: The Emirates–Virgin deal opens interlining for active pharma. A Dubai–US healthcare product could use that capacity.

opportunities.title: Transparent war-risk pricing
opportunities.text: War-risk cover runs at 7–9% of hull value. Customers who see a clear surcharge line are easier to keep than ones hit by surprise.

opportunities.title: East-coast capacity
opportunities.text: DHL is moving toward Khor Fakkan and Fujairah. Early contracts for warehousing and trucking there protect our service.

watchouts.title: Attacks off Dubai
watchouts.text: A projectile exploded near a tanker 50 nautical miles west of Dubai. Jebel Ali calls may face new insurance and routing limits.

watchouts.title: Saudi Red Sea ports in range
watchouts.text: Jazan and Jeddah were struck and shipping lines were told to leave. Sea freight into Saudi via the Red Sea may stall.

watchouts.title: Mines in the strait
watchouts.text: Iran says two more tankers hit mines. Ships not coordinating with Iran face more risk, so fewer will try.

watchouts.title: Oil above $90
watchouts.text: Brent settled at $91.40 on 24 Nov. Fuel surcharges and UAE pump prices for December may rise.

watchouts.title: Margin squeeze
watchouts.text: Our gross margin fell to 21% from 23.2%. Rising war-risk and fuel costs will cut it further if not passed on.

moves.title: Re-route Saudi sea freight to road
moves.text: Call customers shipping into Jeddah and Jazan today and offer a UAE port plus road option into Saudi Arabia.

moves.title: Separate the war-risk line in sea quotes
moves.text: Show war-risk and insurance as their own line in Gulf sea quotes, and shorten validity after the strike off Dubai.

moves.title: Push UAE–Saudi road express
moves.text: Brief e-commerce sellers that Red Sea and air routes into Saudi are under fire and move their volume to road express.

moves.title: Hold peak capacity to 30 November
moves.text: Keep extra riders and sort shifts for noon and Amazon sellers until Sunday, then switch to a returns push.

moves.title: Ask Emirates SkyCargo for Americas block space
moves.text: Request a block space offer on the new Virgin-linked routes and test a healthcare lane to the US.

moves.title: Review fuel surcharge for December
moves.text: With Brent above $90, check our fuel surcharge table before the UAE sets December fuel prices.

note: Read from today's news. Check against our own numbers before acting.
